config/settings.json sets the model. --model beats ANTHROPIC_MODEL, which beats the model key in any file, managed included.
project/.claude/settings.json caps Opus 5.5 at high, replacing that file's top-level maxEffortLevel for this model only. Across files, the lowest cap still applies.
xhigh from project/.claude/settings.local.json runs as high, because maxEffortLevel caps Opus 5.5 at high.

CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL decides the effort. CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL beats --effort, which beats every settings file. A level picked in a running session with /effort sits between the two, and the dashboard can't see it. Among the files, the highest one with a level that counts for the model wins. In one file, the model's modelSettings level beats the top-level effortLevel, and a canonical-name entry beats an alias entry.
Opus 5.5 ignores the top-level effortLevel in config/settings.json. Opus 5.5 and later models take a user settings level only from modelSettings.

Nothing the dashboard reads sets the auto-compact window, so Claude Code uses the window tuned for the model. On Opus 5.5 that window is 1000000 tokens. Only Opus 5.5 was checked, so for any other model the dashboard can't say what the window is. To check, run /autocompact in a new session started in this project.

Nothing the dashboard reads sets the main conversation's cache lifetime, so the plan decides it. On a subscription it's one hour within plan usage, five minutes once usage credits start. On an API key or a cloud provider it's five minutes. The dashboard can't tell when usage credits start. With no plan in the dashboard config, it can't tell the plan either. To check, run claude -p "hello" --output-format json in this project and read usage.cache_creation.
